findings.label: control-flow
findings.failure_mode: a spawn (or other actor) writes/modifies a tracked file inside <tmp> in violation of the instruction-only Bash restriction; git worktree remove --force then silently discards that change with no separate check distinguishing it from the expected untracked graphify-out/ content
evidence: .claude/skills/generate-domain-pack/SKILL.md:31 — bash access "restricted by instruction ... never a write or any other shell command" (not technically enforced)
.claude/skills/generate-domain-pack/SKILL.md:75 — D7 justifies --force only via the untracked graphify-out/ case, no check added for tracked modifications
.claude/skills/generate-domain-pack/SKILL.md:77 — "Run this even if Step 2 or Step 3 failed" forces the unconditional, unchecked discard

findings.label: contract
findings.failure_mode: validate-pack.sh fails on a purely syntactic issue (missing heading, unclosed fence, unwrapped citation); SKILL.md's blanket claim that no such failure is hand-fixable sends the agent back to re-run the whole Step 2 spawn instead of a one-line edit
evidence: .claude/skills/generate-domain-pack/SKILL.md:52 — "none of them fixable by hand-editing ... go back to Step 2"
.claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/validate-pack.sh:19 — missing/renamed heading is a text-shape problem
.claude/skills/pr-review/scripts/validate-pack.sh:81 — unwrapped citation, fixed by adding backticks
.claude/skills/generate-domain-pack/SKILL.md:52 — doc mandates full spawn re-run instead of the trivial fix
